issue.body:
- related: #68232
- related: #68214

## Why

While reviewing https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/71135 and https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/71387, I realized that we should support the async methods for `AssetStateStoreAccessor` following the pattern of `TaskStateStoreAccessor` introduced in #68232.

## How

- Split each sync method into a `_build_*_message` helper plus a shared `_extract_get_response`, then have the sync method `send()` and the new async method `await asend()` the same message. No behaviour change on the sync path.
- `adelete`/`aclear` await `BaseStoreBackend.adelete`/`aclear`, which already exist on the backend base class, and keep the DB-ref-first ordering of their sync counterparts.
- Mirror the four methods on the `AssetStateStoreAccessors` facade. That is the object `TriggerRunner` injects as `trigger_instance.asset_state_store`, so it is what watcher triggers actually call.

## Known gaps (inherited from #68232)

- `BaseStoreBackend` has no async `serialize`/`deserialize` variant, so `aget`/`aset` still call the sync ref (de)serialization on the event-loop thread. With a real-I/O worker backend that can stall the loop despite the async API. Tracked in #72129.
- `adelete`/`aclear` delete the DB ref first, then await `backend.adelete`/`aclear`, which `providers/common/io` raised `NotImplementedError`. Follow-up in #72131.

---

- [x] Yes, with help of Claude Code Opus 5 following [the guidelines](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst#gen-ai-assisted-contributions)

issue.body:
Backport of #72127 to `v3-3-test`.

## Why

Async tasks and watcher triggers need awaitable asset state store accessors so API requests do not block their event loop.

## What

- Backport `aget`, `aset`, `adelete`, and `aclear`, their tests, and documentation.
- Resolve the `context.py` conflict by preserving 3.3's lazy message imports in the shared helpers and moving the shared `ToSupervisor` annotation import under `TYPE_CHECKING`.

## Validation

- All 176 tests in `task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/execution_time/test_context.py` passed in the cached Python 3.10 CI image with this branch's Task SDK, core, shared libraries, and test utilities mounted.
- `prek run --from-ref upstream/v3-3-test --stage pre-commit` passed, including Task SDK mypy. Manual hooks had no applicable checks.
- Fresh Breeze image builds were blocked by Docker Hub timeouts; the tests used the cached image instead. The broader CI suites remain for GitHub Actions.

Inherited backend async limitations are tracked in #72129 and #72131, as in the original PR.

---

- [x] Yes, with help of Codex (GPT-6) following [the guidelines](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst#gen-ai-assisted-contributions)

body:
I have a local read-only candidate: async deserialize hooks preserve the existing instance/thread for sync-only backends, while the object-storage backend provides native reads for an already initialized standard s3fs filesystem with plain/gzip objects. I kept the default hooks on the caller's thread because a thread-bound SQLite custom backend failed under automatic thread offloading. Writes and blocking legacy fallbacks remain unchanged.

With s3fs 2026.9.0 and 75 ms of injected local HTTP latency, ten concurrent task reads completed in a median 940 → 124 ms. SDK/provider HTTP checks cover input lineage on errors, conditional reads when an object changes, and response-body cleanup on cancellation. Focused Airflow timeout/supervisor checks also completed without forced termination. These are controlled local results, not live S3 measurements or the full acceptance matrix. Cold filesystem/credential initialization is still unresolved by this change.

One design choice remains: preserving the S3 read contract currently makes common.io depend on the private `s3fs.core._inner_fetch` helper. Would you consider the async hooks and this narrowly scoped reader together, or prefer a public async read abstraction in the filesystem layer first? Is there an existing implementation I should coordinate with?

issue.title: Allow native async S3 state-store reads

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Async task and asset state-store reads currently call synchronous reference deserialization after awaiting the supervisor response. With an object-storage backend, the read can stall other coroutines on the event loop.

Add non-abstract async reference-read hooks and use them from task and asset `aget`. Their defaults call the existing synchronous hooks on the configured backend instance and caller thread, preserving compatibility with thread-bound custom backends. For an already initialized standard s3fs filesystem, the common.io backend reads plain and gzip objects through the filesystem's existing loop. Unsupported filesystem configurations retain the synchronous path.

**Design feedback requested:** The narrow S3 reader uses the private `s3fs.core._inner_fetch` helper to preserve conditional reads (`If-Match`/`FileExpired`) and response-body cleanup. Is that acceptable here, or should a public async-read abstraction in the filesystem layer come first? A simpler `_cat_file` path lost the existing object-replacement behavior in a controlled test.

This is a read-only partial improvement related to #72129. It does not change `aset`, synchronous callers, blocking fallbacks for custom backends, or cold filesystem/credential initialization. It does not meet the issue's full read/write non-blocking acceptance criteria.

Validation on current `main` (`a52e9f96`):

- Three affected test modules: 294 passed on Python 3.12 in Breeze.
- Local S3-compatible HTTP contract tests: 44 passed, 6 earlier write-experiment cases deselected. They cover task/asset reads, conditional requests, lineage on errors, cancellation cleanup, and loop progress. This is not live AWS validation.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed; provider source-file mypy passed in Breeze. The full manual provider mypy hook could not start because the local `breeze` shim is absent from PATH.
